statement: An international body gains inspection or compute-verification powers covering >= 2 of the top-5 compute jurisdictions (treaty text, official gazettes; by 2029-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met; no body held such powers in 2025. Multilateral activity focused on science and dialogue: the UN General Assembly created an independent scientific panel and a global dialogue on AI governance (no inspection mandate). Bloc B proposed a new world AI cooperation organisation centred on capacity-building and standards. A UN advisory brief and civil-society campaigns (AI red lines) set out verification options, but no treaty text with inspection or compute-verification powers was negotiated.

items.summary: The UN Secretary-General's Scientific Advisory Board issued a science brief on verifying frontier AI. It assessed compute as the most promising verification target (detectable, excludable, quantifiable) and discussed hardware-enabled mechanisms. Advisory only, with no powers.
items.detail: UN SAB, 'Verification of Frontier AI' science brief (file dated 2025-06; exact day not verified).

items.summary: Bloc B's government proposed a new world AI cooperation organisation (tentative headquarters in its largest commercial city), focused on capacity-building, bridging the AI divide and aligning governance rules and standards, alongside a 13-point global AI governance action plan. No inspection or verification mandate was proposed.
items.detail: Premier Li Qiang, WAIC 2025 opening, Shanghai, 2025-07-26; MFA remarks by Ma Zhaoxu (WAICO); Global AI Governance Action Plan. Reuters/Xinhua 2025-07-26.

items.summary: The UN General Assembly established an Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and a Global Dialogue on AI Governance. These are the first universal-membership AI bodies, but their mandate covers assessment and dialogue only, with no inspection or compute-verification powers.
items.detail: UNGA Resolution A/RES/79/325 (2025-08-26), following the Global Digital Compact. First Dialogue scheduled Geneva July 2026.

items.summary: A global call by 200+ public figures (including 10 Nobel laureates), launched at the UN General Assembly, urged governments to agree by end-2026 on internationally binding, verifiable 'red lines' for AI. It is advocacy, not a mandate.
items.detail: Global Call for AI Red Lines (CeSIA, The Future Society, CHAI), launched 2025-09-22 at UNGA80; NBC, Le Monde, El Pais same day.

items.summary: No treaty or agreement in 2025 gave an international body inspection or compute-verification powers over any top-5 compute jurisdiction. Academic proposals (conditional AI-safety treaties, verification frameworks) remained proposals only.
items.detail: E.g. arXiv 2503.18956 (conditional AI safety treaty, Mar 2025); Oxford AIGI 'Verification for International AI Governance' (Jul 2025). Council of Europe AI Convention (2024) has no inspection powers.
